rows.concept: actor state held at the campaign instance

observed.actor_row: Campaign-instance rows (campaign_id>0, 675 rows) carry per-campaign state in three forms: character_data (+ default_character_data merged at read), state_data, and hot columns hp_current/hp_max/armor_class/experience_points/position_q/position_r/position_h3/last_room_id/location_type/location_ref/facing/lifecycle_state/status.
observed.instance_state_data_keys: role, stats, description, content_id, backstory, basicInfo, inventory, resources, psychology, bonds, fears, equipment, motivations, runtime_entity_id, campaign_character_id, senses, skills, abilities, goals, attacks, quests, npc_profile, spells, defenses, actions, features, conditions, ...
observed.runtime_table: dc_campaign_actor_runtime_state (1758 rows, 368 campaigns) entity_payload.state repeats character_data (638), inventory, equipment, resources, currency, conditions, hit_points, spell_slots, focus_points, is_defeated; entity_payload.placement holds room_id, hex, facing, h3_index_res14.
observed.reader: CharacterStateService::getState() reads HP and AC from the instance row hot columns (CharacterStateService.php:147-158), overlays the campaign row state_data (:205), and merges default_character_data under character_data through alias chains. Its persistence path writes state_data and the hot columns together (:1699-1790). The coordinator separately persists dc_campaign_actor_runtime_state through ActorRuntimeMutationService. So the instance row is today's effective home for sheet state, and the runtime table is a second instance-level store.

rows.target_rule: Board directive: per-campaign actor state belongs to the campaign instance of the actor; a template never holds it and a template edit never resets it. Decision (CEO, 2026-11-14): the campaign-instance row is the single home. character_data = pinned canonical actor document. state_data = one typed instance-state document (resources: current/temporary HP, hero points, expended slots, focus, feat resources; progression: XP; flags; campaign role). The row placement columns are the one placement record. Inventory, effects, psychology and social facts keep their domain stores keyed by the instance. hp_current/hp_max/armor_class/level/name/class/ancestry/experience_points columns become same-transaction projections verified equal to their owner. dc_campaign_actor_runtime_state stops owning actor facts: rows that are actors convert to instance rows through explicit migration, rows that are room objects move to the room-state lane, and the table is retired as an actor store. This supersedes the 2026-07-27 choice of that table as actor runtime write authority for actor facts; typed writes, pure reads and no dungeon-blob authority remain binding.
rows.data_impact: Measured 2026-11-14. Only 295 of 675 instance rows join a runtime-state row on (campaign_id, instance_id); 1463 of 1758 runtime rows match no instance row. Among joined rows: runtime HP differs from the instance hot column in 25 NPC rows, runtime placement H3 differs from position_h3 in 205 rows and room in 16; instance state_data HP differs from the hot column in 3 rows. Authored copies largely agree (3 name differences, no level or backstory differences).
rows.recommendation_basis: The instance row is the store the effective-state reader trusts and the only one reliably keyed to an actor row. The runtime table is weakly linked and already divergent, so it should not be chosen as a home for any fact without first reconciling its identity key.
rows.open_item: Classify the 1463 runtime rows that match no instance row (actor needing a row, room object, or orphan of a deleted campaign) before S4 conversion.
